blogs.title: The 0.3 mg Auto-Injector: Is It Enough for a 104 kg Adult?
blogs.description: This blog analyzes the tension between historical auto-injector standards (0.3 mg) and guideline recommendations (0.5 mg for adults >50 kg). Based on case details where adult doses were resupplied as 0.5 mg, we discuss why 0.3 mg devices remain prevalent and how weight-based epinephrine dosing impacts success in severe anaphylaxis.

blogs.title: When Anaphylaxis Strikes Twice: Uncovering Systemic Mastocytosis in the ED
blogs.description: Discussing the diagnostic gray area where a multiphasic reaction does not meet full criteria for mast cell activation, we explore how clinicians can still screen for underlying systemic mastocytosis during workup and why persistent recurrence should raise eyebrows beyond standard allergy testing.

blogs.title: The Steroid Hangover: Why Corticosteroids May Be Harmful in Anaphylaxis
blogs.description: Review the evidence shift in anaphylaxis management regarding corticosteroids. We analyze why traditional 'preventative' dosing (prednisone/dexamethasone) is increasingly discouraged by guidelines despite the 2021 Resuscitation Council UK advice, and how this affects our clinical stewardship.

blogs.title: The Triage Dilemma: ICU vs. Ward for Recurrent Anaphylaxis
blogs.description: Evaluate the decision-making process for patient transfer from the ED to the ICU versus a general ward once symptoms recur. We discuss resource allocation and patient safety thresholds used in the case to determine when multiphasic patients require telemetry-level monitoring.

blogs.title: Tryptase Timing: Why Your Baseline Might Be Wrong in Emergency Settings
blogs.description: A technical breakdown of the correct interval for tryptase testing (1-2 hours from onset vs. >24 hours post-resolution). This post emphasizes how miss-timed samples in acute anaphylaxis scenarios can lead to false negatives in identifying systemic mast cell disorders.

blogs.title: Defining the Fracture: Biphasic vs. Multiphasic Anaphylaxis
blogs.description: Clarify the current definitions in the field: Biphasic (single recurrence) versus Multiphasic (multiple recurrences). We review how doctors need to differentiate true recurrence from sustained response or ongoing absorption, especially as anaphylaxis cases become more complex and atypical.
